_comment: This is Docker's default profile with one deliberate widening: the namespace syscalls stay
allowed, because the inner sandbox is built out of them. The default profile blocks unshare
with CLONE_NEWUSER, and a container running under it would silently lose the nested
confinement -- the parser would run with the container's own network, which is the one thing
That trade is worth stating plainly. Allowing unshare/clone/mount gives a process inside the
container more to work with than the default profile would. What it buys is that the parser --
the only thing here that reads hostile input -- has no network at all, rather than the
container's. docs/23 calls no-egress the single highest-value control in this pipeline, and
this is what pays for it.
The cleaner arrangement, when there is a control plane to drive it, is a separate parser
container with network_mode: none per job, driven over a socket. Then the profile below can go
back to the default and the parser needs no namespace syscalls of its own. See README.md.

syscalls._comment: The namespace and mount calls the inner sandbox needs. Everything else here is the ordinary allow-list.
